about: The game's copy of the clues and explanations, one entry for each group (a field and one of its values). Written from the catalogue on every save. Nobody edits it.

clues.text: Think about things that grow in the ground.
They are alive and they do not walk or fly.
They have roots, stems, and leaves, and they make their own food.

explanation.text: These all grow from the ground and are alive. They make their own food with sunlight. A carrot is a plant, and we eat its orange root.

clues.text: Think about the green part of a plant.
It grows up high, not down in the soil.
We pick it and cook it, but we do not wait for a fruit or a seed.

explanation.text: We eat the green leafy part of these plants. That is why they go together. Spinach has lots of iron in it, which helps your body grow strong.

clues.text: Think about a path that wheels roll along.
This path is made of two long metal lines.
The wheels stay on these lines and cannot go off.

explanation.text: All of these move along metal lines on the ground. They cannot go anywhere else. A train can carry very heavy things, like coal, over long distances.

clues.text: Think about birds that spend lots of time in the water.
These birds find their food in the water.
These birds are not pets and do not live on a farm.

explanation.text: These birds all live near water and find their food there. They are wild birds, not pets or farm animals. Penguins use their flippers to swim underwater, but they cannot fly in the air.

clues.text: Think about something that is alive and can move on its own.
It can find its own food and eat it.
It can have babies, and it breathes and grows.

explanation.text: These all are living things that move, eat and grow. They are not plants, not rocks or water, and not things people make. A giraffe is the tallest animal that lives on land.

clues.text: Think about things you can see outside that are not alive.
These things are not animals and not plants.
People do not make these things; they are just there in the world.

explanation.text: These are all things we find in nature. They are not alive and nobody makes them. A mountain is a very big, high bump on the land.

clues.text: Think about things that are not found growing or walking on their own.
People use their hands and tools to make these things.
These things would not be here if nobody had made them.

explanation.text: These things are all made by people. They are not animals, plants, or things in nature. A bus can carry many people at once.

clues.text: Think about animals that drink their mother's milk when they are babies.
These animals have hair or fur on their bodies.
These animals are warm when you touch them, even when it is cold outside.

explanation.text: They all drink milk from their mothers when they are little, and they have fur or hair. The biggest animal on land is one of these, and it has a long nose called a trunk.

clues.text: Think about animals that have feathers.
These animals have wings and a beak.
Most of them can fly, but some cannot.

explanation.text: They all have feathers and wings. Many of them can fly. A penguin has flippers to swim, but it cannot fly in the air.

clues.text: Think about animals that live in water all the time.
They swim with fins and have a tail for swimming.
They breathe in the water with gills, not air.

explanation.text: These animals all live in water and swim with fins. They breathe using gills. A goldfish can learn to push a small ball under the water.

clues.text: Think about tiny creatures with six legs.
These little creatures often have wings too.
You can see many of them buzzing or crawling near you.

explanation.text: These little creatures all have six legs and a hard shell outside. They have no bones inside. A ladybug has bright red wings with black spots that warn birds to stay away.

clues.text: Think about animals with dry, scaly skin.
These animals often lay eggs on land.
They are cold-blooded and many crawl on their bellies.

explanation.text: They all have dry scaly skin and hatch from eggs. They are all reptiles. A turtle's hard shell keeps it safe from other animals.

clues.text: Think about animals that lived very, very long ago.
These animals are all gone now, and we only see their bones.
Some of these animals were huge, and some had sharp teeth or horns.

explanation.text: These animals all lived long ago and are not alive today. We know about them from their bones. Some of these animals were very big, with long necks and long tails.

clues.text: Think about a dinosaur that eats other animals.
Think about a big animal that hunts its food on the ground.
Think about a hunter with strong legs and sharp teeth that chases other dinosaurs.

explanation.text: These dinosaurs all hunted other animals for food, and they walked and ran on land. The T. rex had a bite so strong it could break the bones of smaller dinosaurs.

clues.text: Think about a dinosaur that eats green plants all day.
This dinosaur walks on the ground and eats plants, not meat.
This plant-eater stays on land and never flies or swims.

explanation.text: All of these dinosaurs stayed on land and ate plants. They did not hunt other animals, fly, or swim. One of these plant-eaters had a long neck to reach leaves high in the trees.

clues.text: Think about animals that can go up in the sky.
These animals had big wings and could fly.
They lived long ago and flew over the land and sea.

explanation.text: These are all flyers. They had wings and could fly in the sky. One of them was as tall as a giraffe when it stood on the ground.

clues.text: Think about animals that live in the water all the time.
These animals move through the water to get around.
They swim in the sea, not walk on land or fly in the sky.

explanation.text: These animals all lived in the water and swam to move around. One of these sea animals had a smaller sea animal inside its tummy!

clues.text: Think about a plant with a big, hard stem called a trunk.
This plant grows very tall and has branches up high.
Birds like to sit and rest in this tall plant.

explanation.text: These all grow tall with a hard trunk and branches up high. They are big plants that live for many years. The coconut tree can grow as tall as 30 metres, which is taller than many houses.

clues.text: Think about the pretty part of a plant that bees visit.
This part is often bright and smells nice.
This part makes seeds after it is done blooming.

explanation.text: These are all flowers. They have pretty petals that make seeds. A sunflower can grow as tall as three metres, taller than a grown-up!

clues.text: Think about plants with long, thin leaves.
These plants grow in big open fields, not in pots.
Many of these plants give us food we eat every day.

explanation.text: These plants all have long, thin leaves and grow close together in fields. We eat them or use them to make food. Bamboo is a giant grass, and it can grow very tall, as tall as a big tree.

clues.text: Think about a plant we grow to eat.
We eat a part of this plant in our meals.
This plant gives us food for our lunch or dinner.

explanation.text: These plants all give us food we can eat. We grow them to eat in our meals. People eat the head of the garlic plant, which grows at the bottom of a long green stalk.

clues.text: Think about what you see when you look up high above your head.
You can see these far above you, but you cannot touch them with your hands.
They are up high in the open air, and you can spot them on a clear day or a dark night.

explanation.text: These are all up high above us, in the open air over our heads. We look up to see them. The Sun is really a star, and it is the star closest to us.

clues.text: Think about something wet you can see outside.
It is not alive, but plants and animals need it.
It can be big or small, and it stays in one place or moves.

explanation.text: They are all wet places in nature. They are not alive, but they are full of water. A river starts small on high ground and gets bigger as it flows down.

clues.text: Think about a place you can walk on, outside.
It is a part of the ground, not water or sky.
You can stand on it and look around.

explanation.text: These are all places on the land where you can go and stand. A hill is smaller than a mountain and not as steep.

clues.text: Think about the hard ground under your feet.
You can pick it up, but it was never alive.
It is not water, not sky, and not a place you live.

explanation.text: These are all bits of the ground. They are not alive and you can touch them. Sand is made of tiny pieces of rock, smaller than gravel.

clues.text: Think about something that takes you from one place to another.
It moves, and it carries people or things.
You can ride in it on land, on water, or in the sky.

explanation.text: All of these carry people or things from one place to another. Some go on roads, some on tracks, some on water, and some in the sky. A ship is a big vehicle that travels on water, and it is bigger than a boat.

clues.text: Think about things you play with.
You hold them, move them, or make them go.
They are made just for fun, not for work.

explanation.text: These are all things you play with. They are made to be fun for children. A paper plane can stay up in the air for almost 28 seconds.

clues.text: Think about things you find inside a home.
These things help us sit, eat, rest, or keep clean.
You use them every day in your own house.

explanation.text: These things all belong in a house. We use them every day for sitting, eating, resting, or cleaning. A sponge has many little holes that help it soak up water and wipe away dirt.

clues.text: Think about something you hold in your hand to help you do work.
It helps you build or fix things.
You use it to make or change things.

explanation.text: These are all tools. People use them to build, fix, or make things. A hammer is used to put nails into wood.

clues.text: Think about places you can go inside or walk on.
People go to these places to do something or to get something.
Some are big and some are small, but people made them all.

explanation.text: People made all of these. We go to them for many things, like praying, learning, shopping or crossing a road. A footbridge is a bridge made just for people to walk on, not for cars.

clues.text: Think about the part of the plant that holds the seeds inside.
We eat this soft, round part that grows after the flower falls.
You can see the little seeds inside when you cut it open.

explanation.text: We eat these soft, ripe parts that grow from flowers. They hold the seeds inside them. A pumpkin is a fruit, and it can be orange, red, blue, or white.

clues.text: Think about the part of a plant that hides in the dark.
This part grows down in the soil, not up in the air.
We dig it out of the ground when we want to eat it.

explanation.text: These plants all keep their tasty part under the ground. We dig them up to eat them. The part of the potato plant that we eat grows under the ground.

clues.text: Think about the little hard parts inside a plant that can grow into a new plant.
We take these out and cook them, not the soft juicy part around them.
We dry them and keep them in jars to eat later, like little hard bits.

explanation.text: We eat the small hard parts of these plants. They are the seeds we cook and eat. A pea you eat is really a tiny seed, and it is very light, less than a small coin's weight.

clues.text: Think about how people go from one place to another.
They move along a hard, flat path.
They have wheels that roll on the ground.

explanation.text: All of these carry people or goods and they roll on wheels along the road. A bicycle has two wheels, and you push the pedals with your feet to make it go.

clues.text: Think about a place where you see lots of water.
This kind of vehicle moves on top of the water.
It can carry people or things across the water.

explanation.text: These all travel on water. They carry people or things across rivers, lakes, and seas. A ship is a big vehicle that travels on water, and it is bigger than a boat.

clues.text: Think about things that go high up, above your head.
These things do not need a road or a track to move.
They move through the sky, up where the birds fly.

explanation.text: These all travel up in the sky, not on the ground or on water. A helicopter can stop and stay still in the air, high above the ground.

clues.text: Think about the things in a house that people use every day.
These things are big and heavy, and they stay in one place.
You sit on them, sleep on them, or keep your things inside them.

explanation.text: These are all big things in a house that people use to sit, sleep, or keep things. A bed can be small for one person or big for two people.

clues.text: Think about what you use when you are hungry or thirsty.
You hold these in your hands at the table.
They help food or drink go into your mouth.

explanation.text: These are all things you use at the table when you eat or drink. You hold them in your hands to help you. A spoon is a tool people use for eating foods that are like liquids, such as soup.

clues.text: Think about things that help make a place clean.
You use them when something is dirty.
They help you wash or sweep away the dirt.

explanation.text: These are all things you use to clean up messes and dirt. A sponge is full of tiny holes that soak up water and dirt.

clues.text: Think about things in your home that need power to work.
They stop working when the power goes off.
You plug them in or switch them on to make them go.

explanation.text: These things all need electricity to work. When you switch them on, they do their job for you. A fridge keeps food cold so it stays good to eat for many days.

clues.text: Think about land that goes up high.
It is much taller than the ground around it.
You would have to climb up to reach the top.

explanation.text: These are all places where the land goes up high. They are tall and steep, not flat. A mountain is a very big, tall bump on the land.

clues.text: Think about a place that goes down, not up.
It is a low or empty spot in the ground.
You can look down into it, and it is not flat or high.

explanation.text: These are all places where the land goes down low. Some are big and some are small. A crater is a round dent on the ground, like a big bowl.

clues.text: Think about an animal that lives in your house with you.
This animal stays close to people and is cared for by them.
People feed it, love it, and it stays in the home.

explanation.text: These animals all live with people in their homes. People feed them and take care of them every day. Dogs like to be near people and are often called a person's best friend.

clues.text: Think about animals that live where people grow food.
These animals are kept by people who work outside in fields.
People raise these animals to help them and to give them things they need.

explanation.text: These animals all live with people on farms. People take care of them and use them for many things. A baby cow can walk just a few minutes after it is born.

clues.text: Think about animals that live far away from people.
They find their own food and make their own homes.
They live on the ground, not in water or in a house.

explanation.text: These animals all live on their own in the wild. They do not live in a house or in water. The giraffe is the tallest animal that lives on land.

clues.text: Think about animals that live in the water.
These animals swim in the big, salty sea.
They are not pets and not farm animals, and they do not live on land.

explanation.text: They all live in the water and are wild animals. They swim in the sea, not in a house or on a farm. A whale breathes air from above the water, just like you and me.

clues.text: Think of a bird that lives in a home with people.
This bird sits in a cage or on a stand inside the house.
People feed it, talk to it, and keep it as a friendly companion.

explanation.text: These birds all live with people in their homes. People feed them and take care of them. Some of these birds can copy the sounds people make.

clues.text: This bird lives near people and gets its food from them.
This bird gives people something to eat or to use.
People keep many of these birds together in one place.

explanation.text: These birds live with people on farms. Farmers feed them and keep them safe. A mother hen lays eggs, and baby chicks come out of the eggs.

clues.text: Think about a bird that lives free, not in a house or a cage.
It flies in the open sky and finds its own food.
It does not live with people or on a farm.
Think about a quiet place where people go to talk to God.
People go there to say thank you or ask for help from God.
People sit or stand together and show love to God there.

explanation.text: These are all special buildings where people go to pray and show love to God. In a temple, people do special things and pray to God.

clues.text: Think about a place where people go to get things.
People give money there and take something home.
It is a busy place where people buy and sell.

explanation.text: In all these places, people go to buy things or sell things. A market is a place where people go to buy or sell things.

clues.text: Think about going from one place to a faraway place.
You go there when you are ready to leave.
You wait there, then you go away on a big trip.

explanation.text: People come to these places to start a trip. They get on a train, plane, or boat and go. The busiest railway station in the world is in Tokyo, Japan.

clues.text: Think about going from one side to the other side.
You do not stay here; you go across or go up.
It helps you get over something, like water or a road.

explanation.text: These are all places where you cross over something or climb up high. You use them to get to the other side or to go up. People have walked across bridges for thousands of years.

clues.text: Think about making something new with your hands.
You put the pieces one on top of another.
When you finish, you have made a shape or a thing.

explanation.text: These toys are for making things. You put the pieces together to build something. You can press the blocks together and they stick, so you can build big things.

clues.text: Think about a toy you hold close and love.
This toy is soft or small, and you use it in your arms or in make-believe.
You hug it, or you act like it is real in a story.

explanation.text: These toys are for hugging and for pretend play. You hold them close or make up stories with them. A teddy bear is a soft toy that looks like a baby bear.

clues.text: Think about something that goes up in the air.
You do not push it or roll it on the ground.
The wind lifts it and carries it up high.

explanation.text: All of these go up in the air and float or glide with the wind. In India, people fly kites on Makar Sankranti.

clues.text: Think about toys that make a sound you can hear.
You blow, bang or pluck it to make the sound.
It makes music, not noise from wheels or wind.

explanation.text: These toys all make music when you blow, bang or pluck them. A recorder is a good instrument for children to learn about music.

clues.text: Think about a very long neck reaching up high.
These dinosaurs had long necks and ate plants all day.
They walked on four legs and stretched their necks to eat leaves.

explanation.text: These dinosaurs all had very long necks and ate plants. They used their long necks to reach leaves high up. One of these dinosaurs, Brachiosaurus, could reach leaves as high as a tall building.

clues.text: Think about a head with something special on top.
Some of these heads have pointy parts sticking out.
Their heads also have a big bony shield behind the pointy parts.

explanation.text: These dinosaurs all have horns and a big bony shield on their heads. That is why they go together in one group. Triceratops had three horns on its head, and its name even means three horned face.

clues.text: Think about the green, leafy food that grows in the ground.
This animal fills its tummy with leaves and grass all day.
It never eats meat or bugs, only green growing things.

explanation.text: All of these animals fill their tummies with leaves and grass. They do not eat other animals. A giraffe is the tallest animal that lives on land.

clues.text: Think about what a hunter catches to eat.
Its food is other animals, not leaves or grass.
It eats nothing but the meat of animals it catches.

explanation.text: These animals all hunt other animals and eat their meat. That is why they belong together. A cheetah can run very fast, as fast as 105 kilometres in one hour.

clues.text: Think about tiny crawling things with six legs.
These animals hunt for very small bugs to fill their tummies.
They use long noses or sticky tongues to catch little bugs.

explanation.text: These animals all get most of their food by eating little bugs. Their bodies help them find and catch them. An anteater's tongue can be as long as a grown-up's arm, and it uses it to lick up ants.

clues.text: Some animals eat green things, and also eat other animals.
This animal fills its tummy with two kinds of food.
It eats leaves or fruit, and also eats small animals.

explanation.text: These animals eat plants and also eat other animals. Both kinds of food go in their tummy. A raccoon eats many things, like fruit, nuts, mice, and insects.

clues.text: Think about a toy you must touch to start its sound.
You do not blow air into it, and you do not press keys.
You tap it, shake it, or bang it, and then it rings out loud.

explanation.text: You make these sounds by hitting or shaking them. Your hand or a stick starts the sound. A tambourine is like a little drum, and it has tiny metal pairs around its edge that jingle.

clues.text: Think about how the air goes in to make the music.
You use your mouth and your breath to play it.
You blow into it, and the air makes the sound.

explanation.text: You play all of these by blowing air into them with your mouth. Your breath makes the music come out. A harmonica is small and you play it by blowing into little holes on its side.

clues.text: Think about how your fingers touch the toy to start the sound.
You move your fingers along tight lines to make the sound.
Your fingers pull or sweep across these lines, and they are not keys or holes.

explanation.text: You make music on these by pulling or sweeping your fingers over tight strings. A harp is a very old string toy; people played it long, long ago in Egypt.

clues.text: Think about a toy you play with your fingers.
You do not hit it or blow it or pull its strings.
You touch its little buttons and music comes out.

explanation.text: You play all of these with your fingers on little parts. When you touch them, music comes out. A toy piano makes its sound from little round metal rods inside, not from strings.
